column1: # Ratchet decay configuration — one row per decayable baseline.
# The ratchets in .githooks/pre-commit are fail-on-GROWTH gates. That freezes
# the level but never lowers it: as of 2026-07-27 every counter below sat at or
# within a rounding error of its ceiling, and src/daemon.c had not moved off
# 14,132 LOC since May. A gate that only fails on growth converges to
# "never worse, never better".
# This file adds the missing second derivative. Two mechanisms, deliberately
# split by blast radius:
#   1. AUTO-LOCK (hard, in pre-commit, no calendar): whenever a counter measures
#      BELOW its baseline, scripts/lib/ratchet.sh rewrites the baseline constant
#      to the measured value and stages it. This replaces the manual
#      "NOTE: lower BASELINE to lock the gain" step that was inconsistently
#      followed. Zero risk: it can only tighten, never block a commit.
#   2. DECAY TARGET (advisory in pre-commit, hard in the weekly CI job): a
#      per-week reduction the counter is expected to meet. Missing it never
#      blocks a commit or the merge queue — .claude/rules/ci-required-checks.md
#      makes these gates blocking, and session-worktree-isolation.md records that
#      a hard gate "would have blocked the same day's three urgent red-CI fixes".
#      Instead scripts/ratchet-debt-report.sh fails, and the weekly workflow
#      files/updates one durable GitHub issue naming the debt.
# RATE semantics:
#   auto   — derive the rate from this counter's OWN git history (see
#            ratchet-debt-report.sh). The target is a fraction of the velocity
#            the counter has actually demonstrated, so it is achievable by
#            construction rather than invented. Preferred.
#   <N>    — fixed units per week. Use only when history is too short to fit.
#   off    — participate in auto-lock but set no decay target.
# FLOOR: decay stops here. Use the target documented in the matching
# .claude/rules/*.md where one exists; `none` where the rules file states no
# endpoint — inventing one would be a number without a measurement.
# PATTERN: grep -E pattern selecting this ratchet's output line from its script's
# stdout. Required because check-agent-core-boundary.sh emits two counters, and
# because the scripts phrase their counts differently ("N (ceiling B)" vs
# "= N LOC (ceiling B)"). The report reads the integer immediately preceding
# "(ceiling" on the matched line.
